system.description: Your own two hands.
Brass, bought "as a paperweight" off a stall in Ridley Road. Illegal to carry.
Swung from the hand. Doubles as a lock nobody trusts.
Improvised and nasty. A hit that does any damage also causes Bleeding. Smashes on a Proper Mess.
From the pub. Long reach, snaps easily.
Doubles as a tool: it opens a cheap door (Graft, one band easier).
Willow. Kept in the car "for the nets".
Aluminium. Nobody in Hackney has ever played baseball.
Opens doors, shutters and skulls. Counts as a tool for breaking in.
A seven iron from a bag in a Range Ruler boot.
Carrying one is a crime on its own if you are searched. A Smashed It hit causes Bleeding.
Folds into a pocket. Still a knife to the custody sergeant. A Smashed It hit causes Bleeding.
Serrated, green-handled, banned. Everyone who sees it calls the police. A Smashed It hit causes Bleeding.
Big, ugly, illegal. Draws attention the moment it comes out.
Off the wall of a stairwell. Through a door in one swing.
A rusty little automatic. Small, quiet for a gun, unreliable.
A blank-firer drilled out in a garage in Leyton. Jams on a Proper Mess.
A proper modern 9mm. Comes in a sock, never asked about.
An old .38, somebody's granddad's from the war. Six shots, never jams.
A chromed .50 that kicks like a horse. Off Your Game for anyone with Muscle d4.
A converted Mac-style machine pistol. Can fire a burst.
Compact, sprays more than it aims. Can fire a burst.
Met ARV issue. Never for sale; taken off a Trojan unit at your peril.
Two barrels, short range, very loud. At Engaged range it adds +2 impact.
Six in the tube. Clears a room and wakes the street.
A legal-ish double-barrel from Essex. Licensed to someone else.
For pigeons. Still gets you nicked if you point it at someone.
Bolt action with a scope. Hits anything you can see.
An AK that came in a lorry of washing machines. Can fire a burst.
Met ARV carbine. Never for sale.
Every building site in E9 has a pile.
Aimed down a street on bonfire night. Also a decent distraction.
A milk bottle, petrol and a rag. A hit sets the target Burning; a miss sets fire to whatever is next to them.
Fills the area: everyone in it is Gassed and nobody can be targeted from outside until it clears.
Hits everyone Engaged with the target too. Where did you even get this?
Police issue. Everyone Engaged with the target is Stunned.
Police issue. A hit also inflicts Stunned and Prone.
Police issue. A hit inflicts Gassed.
Police issue.
GM only. If one of these turns up in Hackney, the whole Met turns up after it. Hits everyone Engaged with the target.
A box of a hundred. Fits the Pocket .22.
A box of fifty. Fits the Converted Pistol, Polymer Nine, Machine Pistol and Micro SMG.
A box of fifty for the Service Revolver.
Twenty for the Hand Cannon. Each one costs six quid.
A box of twenty-five cartridges for any shotgun.
Thirty for the Kalash.
Twenty for the Hunting Rifle.
A tin of five hundred.
Police issue. Never sold.
Police issue. Never sold.
Police carbine magazine. Never sold.
One rocket for the launcher. GM only. Never sold.
Thick enough to take the edge off a punch.
Old-school. Takes the edge off a knife and a slide down the tarmac.
Leathers and a lid. Reduction 2, and coming off a bike does half damage.
Covert vest under a hoodie. Police wear the hi-vis version.
Covert body armour. Stops a pistol round; you still feel it.
Met-pattern body armour.
TSG kit. +3 Guard while you hold it; you cannot use a two-handed weapon.
Cut cable locks and cheap D-locks: bike locks are one band easier.
Through any bike lock in seconds: two bands easier. Shrieks — anyone near notices.
Clones keyless-entry fobs from the doorstep: car locks two bands easier, silently.
Plugs into the OBD port and teaches the car a new key. Car locks two bands easier and the car starts clean (no hotwire).
Old-school door opener: older cars one band easier.
For the ignition barrel. No easier, but you can try.
For doors and padlocks: one band easier, and silent.
Slow and quiet. Gets through a padlock hasp or a cheap chain given a minute.
Patch up a motor: a Graft roll (Medium) restores Body (Sorted 2, Smashed It 4, Legendary all) or fixes a flat tyre.
Five litres. Refuels a vehicle, or makes three Petrol Bombs with some milk bottles.
A pair of number plates off a written-off car. Swap them (Graft, Easy) and the police scanner reads the new plate.
Tag a wall, or cover a stolen bike's frame so it is not recognised.
Pay-as-you-go, no contract. Pat only texts this number.
Listen to the Met on an old Airwave scanner: Savvy steps up one die to spot police coming, and you hear when the helicopter goes up.
Watch a target from a rooftop. Savvy one band easier for casing a job.
Bright LED torch. Also good for blinding someone for a moment (Front vs their Bottle).
A pack of heavy-duty ties. Restrain a Grabbed or Down person: they are Cuffed.
Fixes everything. Silences everyone.
A good fake driving licence: Front steps up one die when the police ask who you are.
Topped up. Get on a bus without paying cash.
Hides your face. Witnesses can't describe you: a witnessed crime adds 1 less Heat (minimum 0) while you wear it — but wearing one in daylight is a look.
A decent D-lock for your own ride. Locked bikes need a Hard roll to nick.

A ten-pound bag. Take it: Blazed (+1 Bottle, -1 Savvy and Wheels), then Foggy.

Caught with a bag: a caution and +0 Heat. Caught with a lot of it: that is dealing.

A gram wrap. Take it: Wired (+1 Front and Bottle), then Crashing.

Caught carrying: +1 Heat.

Pressed pills stamped with a logo. Take one: Loved Up (+2 Front, -1 Aim and Savvy), then Wrung Out.

Caught carrying: +1 Heat.
Street Xanax. Take one: Numb (Shaken and Bricking It stop working; -1 Moves and Aim), then Jittery.
A balloon of laughing gas. Giggling for a couple of minutes (-2 Savvy, -1 Front). The canisters litter every park in E9.
Gym-bought steroids. Take a course: Pumped (+1 Muscle, -1 Front), then Roid Rage.
Patch Up (Savvy, Medium) removes Bleeding or Hurt and heals 2. Three uses.
Stops Bleeding. No roll needed if nobody is hitting you.
Co-codamol from the chemist: Numbed (In Pain and Hurt stop working) for an hour, and removes In Pain.
Buzzing (+1 Moves) for half an hour and removes Knackered.
A four-pack. One can: Dutch Courage (+1 Bottle). A second while you have it: Mullered.
Removes Gassed.
Removes Shaken. Twenty in a pack.
A sandwich, crisps and a drink. Heals 1.
Four wings and chips from Chicken Palace. Heals 2.
Large doner, chilli sauce. Heals 2 and removes Mullered.
At Uncle's Cafe. Heals 4 and removes Bruised and Knackered.
With liquor, from the shop on Broadway Market. Heals 3 and removes Shaken.
Grey trackies and a hoodie. You look like everyone else on the estate.
Head to toe in black. Witnesses cannot describe you, but anyone who sees you assumes the worst.

system.when: Walking in like you are meant to be there
system.description: Nobody stops a man in hi-vis. Front steps up one die to walk in somewhere like you are meant to be there.

system.when: Going unnoticed on the street
system.description: Teal or orange, with the box. Invisible on any street in London.

system.when: Dealing with posh people or getting waved through
system.description: A sharp suit. Front steps up one die with anyone posh, and the police wave you through.
Home kit. On match day you are one of forty thousand.

system.when: Getting into a hospital or past a cordon
system.description: Green Capital Ambulance uniform, borrowed from a locker. Walk into any A&E. Impersonation if caught.

system.when: Giving orders to civilians
system.description: A Metro Police uniform. The biggest blag in London, and the biggest crime if you are caught (+2 Heat).

system.when: Cutting a lock or hotwiring
system.description: You know every lock on the market. Graft steps up one die when you nick a bicycle or scooter.

system.when: Losing a pursuer
system.description: Wheels steps up one die in a chase while you are the one being chased.

system.when: Finding a way, a shortcut or a person in Hackney
system.description: Savvy steps up one die anywhere on the Hackney maps.

system.when: Talking to the police
system.description: Front steps up one die when talking your way out of a stop or an arrest.

system.when: Climbing, vaulting, leg it on foot
system.description: Moves steps up one die when running from someone or going over walls.

system.when: Fighting hand to hand
system.description: Muscle steps up one die in a punch-up with no weapons.

system.when: Driving a taxi
system.description: You did The Knowledge. Wheels steps up one die on taxi jobs, and fares tip more.

system.when: First aid and treating patients
system.description: Savvy steps up one die for first aid and paramedic jobs.

system.when: Riding anything on two wheels
system.description: Wheels steps up one die on a bike, scooter or motorbike.

system.when: Fixing, modding or stripping a motor
system.description: Graft steps up one die working on any vehicle, including a toolkit repair.

system.when: An aimed shot after taking a moment
system.description: Aim steps up one die when you spend an action aiming first.

system.when: Firing a burst
system.description: Aim steps up one die when you fire a burst.

system.when: Grabbing, headbutts and fighting dirty
system.description: Muscle steps up one die to grab someone, break a hold or fight dirty.

system.when: Running from the police on foot
system.description: Moves steps up one die to escape a police stop or a foot chase.

system.when: Taking a hit or staying conscious
system.description: Grit steps up one die to stay conscious, shrug off pain or keep going hurt.

system.when: Spotting tails and police after dark
system.description: Savvy steps up one die at night.

system.when: Spotting undercover police and informers
system.description: Savvy steps up one die to clock a plain-clothes officer or a grass.

system.when: Bluffing your way in
system.description: Front steps up one die to lie your way past a door, a desk or a cordon.

system.when: Haggling, buying and selling
system.description: Front steps up one die when you haggle; shops knock 10% off for you.

system.when: Intimidation when you do not care
system.description: Bottle steps up one die to face someone down or scare them off.

system.when: Keeping calm under fire
system.description: Bottle steps up one die when you are being shot at or chased.

system.when: Sneaking and staying unseen
system.description: Moves steps up one die to slip past someone, and you lose Heat 15 seconds faster.

system.when: Deliveries on time
system.description: Wheels steps up one die on courier jobs, and late deliveries still pay full.

system.when: Driving under blue lights
system.description: Wheels steps up one die driving an emergency vehicle with its lights on.

system.when: Knowing how the police work
system.description: You used to be in the job. Savvy steps up one die to predict what the police will do next.

system.when: Finding someone who sells what you need
system.description: Savvy steps up one die to find a seller, a buyer or a bent professional.
Issued equipment for police NPCs and duty scenarios.
Rare, illegal and loud. Firing it is a serious escalation; witnessed shots add two Heat.
Armed response equipment. The GM controls its availability.
Police scenario equipment. On a hit the GM may choose Stunned or Restrained from the condition catalogue.
One improvised throw. Remove it from your kit after use.
Issued to armed units; conspicuous on the street.
A thick work coat. Better than a T-shirt when trouble starts.
Makes a lock two bands easier. Loud: a merely Sorted result can attract witnesses.
An improvised tool. No automatic difficulty reduction.
A proper duty bag, including the kit needed for the patient minigame. No substitute for reaching A&E.
Helmet, gloves and protective clothing for the fire minigame. Do not model real emergency procedures from these game rules.
Your Blower. Messages, maps, shifts and Auntie Pat. No battery bookkeeping.
A dispatch radio for service shifts; calls also appear in the Blower.
A bike lock and a plausible reason to be crouching beside a bicycle.
Sometimes the most convincing disguise in London. Circumstantial benefits are agreed with the GM.
Practical protection. Does not stack another mechanical armour bonus.
Big, waterproof, covered in reflective tape.
Apply Cuffed after a successful arrest or fictional restraint. The condition prevents driving.
A Graft check can repair 2 Body with a safe location, time and parts; the GM adjudicates major wrecks.
Change your description at a market. Use the local service in the Blower.
A beam under the arches and into the back of the wrong van.
Story prop. A respray service abstracts the mechanical marker reset; no real evasion procedure is described.
